amendments.rule: An attributive demonstrative supplies the English determiner, so the article governing that noun is its own `unrepresented` unit. `τὸν ναὸν τοῦτον` → *this temple* and `ὁ ναὸς οὗτος` → *this temple* both give *this* to the demonstrative and nothing to the article, as `τὴν ἡμέραν ἐκείνην` → *that day*, `ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ` → *in that hour*, and `ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις` → *in those days* do. Whether the demonstrative precedes or follows the article makes no difference. This is rule 20's displacement holding for a demonstrative rather than a possessive: another source word already occupies the English determiner slot, so the article realizes nothing. Do not supply the article a *the* the ASV never wrote, and do not split *this* or *that* across the demonstrative and the article. Where the ASV writes a **multiword** determiner expression for the demonstrative, that expression is the demonstrative's whole and the article still realizes nothing: `ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ` → *the same hour* gives *the same* to `ἐκείνῃ`, headed on *same* and never on *the*, and leaves the article `unrepresented`, exactly as the substantival `αὕτη` → *The same* takes both words under rule 49. That is rule 49's clause holding for an attributive demonstrative — a demonstrative takes the whole English expression the ASV builds for it — so a written *the* is not evidence that the article is realized, and the count of English words is not the test here that rules 50 and 94 make it elsewhere. What the article may not be given is a determiner that some other source word's own English already spells. Rule 60 is the contrast and its test is unchanged: where no Greek demonstrative competes, a supplied demonstrative determiner is the article's own to take, which is why `αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ` → *that very hour* gives *that* to the article and *very* to the intensive pronoun. Rule 22 is not the contrast, because a substantival article governs no head noun; where the demonstrative stands alone, as `ταῦτα` → *these things*, no article is in question at all.
amendments.why: Rule 38 tells a reader not to supply the article a *the* the ASV never wrote, but says nothing about the case where the ASV does write one inside a two-word demonstrative expression, and its closing prohibition names only the one-word *this* and *that*. ACT.16.33's `ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ` → *the same hour* is exactly that gap, and the verse pass read the written *the* as evidence that the article was realized — against rule 38's own cited example of this very Greek phrase. The amendment closes the gap with rule 49's reasoning, which already gives a demonstrative the whole English expression built for it, and it names rule 60's boundary so that the neighbouring `αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ` → *that very hour* at ACT.16.18 stays decided the other way. Returned as an amendment rather than a new rule because the over-broad sentence is inside rule 38 and a later reader meeting *the same* would read that sentence first.

conventions: A preverb particle the ASV writes as a separate word stays inside the compound verb's own unit where the governing preposition is ἀπό, whose English here is a bare of or from and does not carry the particle: ἐξελθεῖν ἀπ᾽ αὐτῆς → to come out of her (16.18) gives out to the verb and of to ἀπό, as ἀπελθεῖν ἀπὸ τῆς πόλεως → to go away from the city (16.39) and ἐξελθόντες ἀπὸ τῆς φυλακῆς → they went out of the prison (16.40) do. Rule 106's contrary arm is scoped to a preposition whose own gloss carries the particle, as ἐκ → out of does; where the preposition's gloss is the whole English expression the verb goes bare, which is why εἰσελθόντες εἰς → come and into (16.15) and εἰσῆλθον πρός → entered and into (16.40) leave the verb only its verb word.

τις with an anarthrous noun keeps whatever indefinite word the ASV writes for it, and the noun receives a supplied determiner only where a second English word is left over for it. a certain disciple (16.1) and a certain maid (16.16) give certain to τις and the discontinuous a … disciple and a … maid to the noun under rule 51; a man of Macedonia (16.9), where the ASV writes only one determiner, gives a to τις and leaves ἀνήρ bare. Leaving τις unrepresented and reading the single a as a rule 51 helper on the noun remains defensible, but no contentful indefinite in this chapter is left empty.

report: Checked all 76 candidate lemma groups and read the dump end to end for added-side asymmetries the table is blind to. Two real splits; both patched.

Split 1, attributive demonstrative. ACT.16.12, 16.17, 16.20, 16.35 and 16.38 all leave the article unrepresented under rule 38; ACT.16.33 alone gave τῇ → the and ἐκείνῃ → same, on the ground that the ASV wrote the determiner expression as two words. Nothing in the source licenses that, and ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ is rule 38's own cited example. Patched so that ἐκείνῃ takes the same headed on same and τῇ is unrepresented, matching this chapter's own αὕτη → The same at 16.17.

Split 2, supplied object pronoun. ACT.16.14 (heard us), 16.15 (besought us), 16.23 (cast them) and 16.39 (asked them) all fold a supplied object onto the verb that requires it in English, as rule 74 requires. ACT.16.37 alone stretched the second us (t019, object of have cast) back onto ἡμᾶς in the preceding participial clause, though ἔβαλαν there is the same lemma and the same objectless construction as ἔβαλον at 16.23. Patched: ἡμᾶς keeps t009 only, and t019 rides with ἔβαλαν.

Non-splits worth naming so a later reader does not reopen them. The ὁ T→PREP and T→V buckets look inconsistent and are not: 16.2 gives the article the discontinuous the … that because it precedes its noun, 16.4 gives it only that because it follows, 16.32 gives it that alone because it is substantival before a prepositional phrase, and 16.14 splits unto the things from which were spoken because a participle follows. Rules 31 and 32 decide each by configuration. The preverb treatment before ἀπό is uniform across 16.18, 16.39 and 16.40. The τις groups differ only in how many English determiner words the ASV wrote, and 16.27 against 16.29 differs only in whether the ASV wrote a copular being.

BSB: 617/626 comparable, nine disagreements, none a genuine error. Seven are the documented article and preposition conventions (16.12, 16.14, 16.19, 16.22, 16.25, 16.33 ἐν, 16.33 οἱ) under rules 20, 23, 36 and 38. 16.9 καί is the ASV writing a single and for two coordinating conjunctions, so one of them has no English word. 16.29 γενόμενος is empty because the ASV renders ἔντρομος γενόμενος by trembling for fear alone, exactly as 16.27 gives ἔξυπνος the lexical content and γενόμενος only the written being. No accepted edge was changed to move that figure.
The 16.33 patch adds a tenth BSB disagreement, τῇ, on the same rule 38 convention. That is expected and is not a correction.

One amendment (rule 38, multiword determiner expressions), two conventions, no new rules. The chapter's other recurring judgments — supplied object pronouns, supplied when on participles, case prepositions riding with the article — are restatements of rules 7, 21, 74 and 86 and are not logged.
